sanskrit: akṣataḥ śastrasaṃpanno jitāriḥ saha rājabhiḥ ratham āsthāya taṃ divyaṃ nirjagāma girivrajāt
english: Uninjured, well-armed, his enemies conquered, accompanied by the kings, he mounted that divine chariot and departed from Girivraja.

sanskrit: yaḥ sa sodaryavān nāma dviyodhaḥ kṛṣṇasārathiḥ abhyāsaghātī saṃdṛśyo durjayaḥ sarvarājabhiḥ
english: That chariot, famed as Sodaryavān, capable of dual combat, with Kṛṣṇa as its charioteer — terrible in appearance and unconquerable by all kings.

sanskrit: bhīmārjunābhyāṃ yodhābhyām āsthitaḥ kṛṣṇasārathiḥ śuśubhe rathavaryo 'sau durjayaḥ sarvadhanvibhiḥ
english: Mounted by warriors Bhīma and Arjuna, with Kṛṣṇa as its charioteer, that foremost chariot shone splendidly — unconquerable by all archers.

sanskrit: śakraviṣṇū hi saṃgrāme ceratus tārakāmaye rathena tena taṃ kṛṣṇa upāruhya yayau tadā
english: For Indra and Viṣṇu had roamed on that very chariot in the battle of the gods against the demons, known as Tārakāmaya; mounting it, Kṛṣṇa now proceeded.

sanskrit: taptacāmīkarābheṇa kiṅkiṇījālamālinā meghanirghoṣanādena jaitreṇāmitraghātinā
english: Gleaming like refined gold, adorned with a garland of small bells, thundering with the roar of clouds — that victorious chariot, the slayer of foes.

sanskrit: yena śakro dānavānāṃ jaghāna navatīr nava taṃ prāpya samahṛṣyanta rathaṃ te puruṣarṣabhāḥ
english: With that chariot Indra had slain ninety-nine times nine of the demons; obtaining it, those bulls among men rejoiced greatly.

sanskrit: tataḥ kṛṣṇaṃ mahābāhuṃ bhrātṛbhyāṃ sahitaṃ tadā rathasthaṃ māgadhā dṛṣṭvā samapadyanta vismitāḥ
english: Then the Māgadha people, seeing the mighty-armed Kṛṣṇa together with the two brothers standing on that chariot, were struck with astonishment.

sanskrit: hayair divyaiḥ samāyukto ratho vāyusamo jave adhiṣṭhitaḥ sa śuśubhe kṛṣṇenātīva bhārata
english: Yoked with divine horses, equal to the wind in speed, that chariot, presided over by Kṛṣṇa, shone exceedingly, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: asaṅgī devavihitas tasmin rathavare dhvajaḥ yojanād dadṛśe śrīmān indrāyudhasamaprabhaḥ
english: The banner fixed by the gods on that foremost chariot, unimpeded, could be seen from a yojana away, glorious, blazing like Indra's rainbow.

sanskrit: cintayām āsa kṛṣṇo 'tha garutmantaṃ sa cābhyayāt kṣaṇe tasmin sa tenāsīc caityayūpa ivocchritaḥ
english: Then Kṛṣṇa thought of Garuḍa, and Garuḍa immediately came to him; in that instant, perched on the banner, he stood like a tall sacrificial post.

sanskrit: vyāditāsyair mahānādaiḥ saha bhūtair dhvajālayaiḥ tasthau rathavare tasmin garutmān pannagāśanaḥ
english: With wide-open mouths and mighty roars, accompanied by spirits who dwell in banners, Garuḍa the serpent-devourer stood on that foremost chariot.

sanskrit: durnirīkṣyo hi bhūtānāṃ tejasābhyadhikaṃ babhau āditya iva madhyāhne sahasrakiraṇāvṛtaḥ
english: Difficult for any being to gaze upon, he blazed with surpassing brilliance, like the sun at midday encompassed by a thousand rays.

sanskrit: na sa sajjati vṛkṣeṣu śastraiś cāpi na riṣyate divyo dhvajavaro rājan dṛśyate devamānuṣaiḥ
english: It does not catch on trees, nor is it harmed by weapons — that divine foremost banner, O king, is visible to gods and humans alike.

sanskrit: tam āsthāya rathaṃ divyaṃ parjanyasamanisvanam niryayau puruṣavyāghraḥ pāṇḍavābhyāṃ sahācyutaḥ
english: Mounting that divine chariot whose rumble was like a rain-cloud, the tiger among men, Acyuta, set forth together with the two Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: yaṃ lebhe vāsavād rājā vasus tasmād bṛhadrathaḥ bṛhadrathāt krameṇaiva prāpto bārhadrathaṃ nṛpam
english: The chariot that King Vasu had received from Vāsava (Indra), from him Bṛhadratha obtained it, and from Bṛhadratha it had passed in succession to the king descended from Bṛhadratha — Jarāsaṃdha.

sanskrit: sa niryayau mahābāhuḥ puṇḍarīkekṣaṇas tataḥ girivrajād bahis tasthau same deśe mahāyaśāḥ
english: The mighty-armed, lotus-eyed one of great fame then departed and halted outside Girivraja on level ground.

sanskrit: tatrainaṃ nāgarāḥ sarve satkāreṇābhyayus tadā brāhmaṇapramukhā rājan vidhidṛṣṭena karmaṇā
english: There all the townspeople, with brāhmaṇas at their head, O king, came to honor him with proper rites as prescribed.

sanskrit: bandhanād vipramuktāś ca rājāno madhusūdanam pūjayām āsur ūcuś ca sāntvapūrvam idaṃ vacaḥ
english: The kings, freed from captivity, worshipped Madhusūdana and spoke these soothing words to him:

sanskrit: naitac citraṃ mahābāho tvayi devakinandana bhīmārjunabalopete dharmasya paripālanam
english: "This is no wonder, O mighty-armed one, O son of Devakī — that you, endowed with the strength of Bhīma and Arjuna, uphold dharma.

sanskrit: jarāsaṃdhahrade ghore duḥkhapaṅke nimajjatām rājñāṃ samabhyuddharaṇaṃ yad idaṃ kṛtam adya te
english: That you have today rescued these kings who were sinking in the terrible lake of Jarāsaṃdha, the mire of suffering —

sanskrit: viṣṇo samavasannānāṃ giridurge sudāruṇe diṣṭyā mokṣād yaśo dīptam āptaṃ te puruṣottama
english: O Viṣṇu, of those who were crushed in the terrible mountain-fortress, by good fortune glory blazing from their liberation has been won by you, O best of men.

sanskrit: kiṃ kurmaḥ puruṣavyāghra bravīhi puruṣarṣabha kṛtam ity eva taj jñeyaṃ nṛpair yady api duṣkaram
english: What shall we do, O tiger among men? Speak, O bull among men — whatever you say must be understood as already accomplished by us kings, even if it be difficult."

sanskrit: tān uvāca hṛṣīkeśaḥ samāśvāsya mahāmanāḥ yudhiṣṭhiro rājasūyaṃ kratum āhartum icchati
english: Hṛṣīkeśa, the great-souled one, reassuring them, said: "Yudhiṣṭhira wishes to perform the Rājasūya sacrifice."

sanskrit: tasya dharmapravṛttasya pārthivatvaṃ cikīrṣataḥ sarvair bhavadbhir yajñārthe sāhāyyaṃ dīyatām iti
english: "For him who is devoted to dharma and desires sovereignty, let all of you give your assistance for the purpose of that sacrifice."

sanskrit: tataḥ pratītamanasas te nṛpā bharatarṣabha tathety evābruvan sarve pratijajñuś ca tāṃ giram
english: Then those kings, O bull of the Bhāratas, with satisfied minds all said "So be it" and pledged their word to that.

sanskrit: ratnabhājaṃ ca dāśārhaṃ cakrus te pṛthivīśvarāḥ kṛcchrāj jagrāha govindas teṣāṃ tadanukampayā
english: Those lords of the earth made the Dāśārha (Kṛṣṇa) a recipient of their jewels; out of compassion for them, Govinda accepted their gifts with some reluctance.

sanskrit: jarāsaṃdhātmajaś caiva sahadevo mahārathaḥ niryayau sajanāmātyaḥ puraskṛtya purohitam
english: And Sahadeva, the great chariot-warrior son of Jarāsaṃdha, came out with his kinsmen and ministers, placing his priest before him.

sanskrit: sa nīcaiḥ praśrito bhūtvā bahuratnapurogamaḥ sahadevo nṛṇāṃ devaṃ vāsudevam upasthitaḥ
english: Bowing low, with many jewels preceding him, Sahadeva approached Vāsudeva, the god among men.

sanskrit: bhayārtāya tatas tasmai kṛṣṇo dattvābhayaṃ tadā abhyaṣiñcata tatraiva jarāsaṃdhātmajaṃ tadā
english: Then Kṛṣṇa, granting him freedom from fear, thereupon consecrated the son of Jarāsaṃdha as king right there.

sanskrit: gatvaikatvaṃ ca kṛṣṇena pārthābhyāṃ caiva satkṛtaḥ viveśa rājā matimān punar bārhadrathaṃ puram
english: Having achieved accord with Kṛṣṇa and being honored by the two Pārthas, that wise king re-entered the city of Bārhadratha.

sanskrit: kṛṣṇas tu saha pārthābhyāṃ śriyā paramayā jvalan ratnāny ādāya bhūrīṇi prayayau puṣkarekṣaṇaḥ
english: But Kṛṣṇa, the lotus-eyed, blazing with supreme splendor, taking abundant jewels, set forth together with the two Pārthas.

sanskrit: indraprastham upāgamya pāṇḍavābhyāṃ sahācyutaḥ sametya dharmarājānaṃ prīyamāṇo 'bhyabhāṣata
english: Arriving at Indraprastha together with the two Pāṇḍavas, Acyuta, delighted, met the Dharma-king and spoke to him.

sanskrit: diṣṭyā bhīmena balavāñ jarāsaṃdho nipātitaḥ rājāno mokṣitāś ceme bandhanān nṛpasattama
english: "By good fortune the mighty Jarāsaṃdha has been felled by Bhīma, and these kings have been freed from their bonds, O best of kings.

sanskrit: diṣṭyā kuśalinau cemau bhīmasenadhanaṃjayau punaḥ svanagaraṃ prāptāv akṣatāv iti bhārata
english: By good fortune these two, Bhīmasena and Dhanaṃjaya, have returned safely to their own city, unhurt, O Bhārata."

sanskrit: tato yudhiṣṭhiraḥ kṛṣṇaṃ pūjayitvā yathārhataḥ bhīmasenārjunau caiva prahṛṣṭaḥ pariṣasvaje
english: Then Yudhiṣṭhira, honoring Kṛṣṇa as he deserved, and embracing Bhīmasena and Arjuna, was filled with joy.

sanskrit: tataḥ kṣīṇe jarāsaṃdhe bhrātṛbhyāṃ vihitaṃ jayam ajātaśatrur āsādya mumude bhrātṛbhiḥ saha
english: Then, with Jarāsaṃdha destroyed, Ajātaśatru, having obtained the victory accomplished by his brothers, rejoiced together with his brothers.

sanskrit: yathāvayaḥ samāgamya rājabhis taiś ca pāṇḍavaḥ satkṛtya pūjayitvā ca visasarja narādhipān
english: Meeting those kings according to their age, the Pāṇḍava honored and worshipped them duly, then dismissed those lords of men.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhirābhyanujñātās te nṛpā hṛṣṭamānasāḥ jagmuḥ svadeśāṃs tvaritā yānair uccāvacais tataḥ
english: Dismissed by Yudhiṣṭhira, those kings, with joyful hearts, quickly departed to their own kingdoms in various conveyances.

sanskrit: evaṃ puruṣaśārdūlo mahābuddhir janārdanaḥ pāṇḍavair ghātayām āsa jarāsaṃdham ariṃ tadā
english: Thus the tiger among men, the greatly wise Janārdana, caused the enemy Jarāsaṃdha to be slain through the Pāṇḍavas at that time.

sanskrit: ghātayitvā jarāsaṃdhaṃ buddhipūrvam ariṃdamaḥ dharmarājam anujñāpya pṛthāṃ kṛṣṇāṃ ca bhārata
english: Having intentionally caused Jarāsaṃdha to be slain, that subduer of foes took leave of the Dharma-king and of Pṛthā and Kṛṣṇā (Draupadī), O Bhārata.

sanskrit: subhadrāṃ bhīmasenaṃ ca phalgunaṃ yamajau tathā dhaumyam āmantrayitvā ca prayayau svāṃ purīṃ prati
english: Taking leave also of Subhadrā, Bhīmasena, Phalguna (Arjuna), the twin brothers, and Dhaumya, he set out for his own city.

sanskrit: tenaiva rathamukhyena taruṇādityavarcasā dharmarājavisṛṣṭena divyenānādayan diśaḥ
english: On that very foremost chariot, blazing like the young sun, dispatched by the Dharma-king, he made the directions resound with its divine roar.

sanskrit: tato yudhiṣṭhiramukhāḥ pāṇḍavā bharatarṣabha pradakṣiṇam akurvanta kṛṣṇam akliṣṭakāriṇam
english: Then the Pāṇḍavas, with Yudhiṣṭhira at their head, O bull of the Bhāratas, circumambulated Kṛṣṇa the effortless doer in a rightward direction.

sanskrit: tato gate bhagavati kṛṣṇe devakinandane jayaṃ labdhvā suvipulaṃ rājñām abhayadās tadā
english: Then, after the blessed Kṛṣṇa, the son of Devakī, had departed — having won a great victory, the giver of safety to kings —

sanskrit: saṃvardhitaujaso bhūyaḥ karmaṇā tena bhārata draupadyāḥ pāṇḍavā rājan parāṃ prītim avardhayan
english: Their energy further heightened by that deed, O Bhārata, the Pāṇḍavas, O king, increased the great joy of Draupadī.

sanskrit: tasmin kāle tu yad yuktaṃ dharmakāmārthasaṃhitam tad rājā dharmataś cakre rājyapālanakīrtimān
english: In that time the king, renowned for protecting his kingdom, rightfully did what was fitting, encompassing dharma, pleasure, and wealth.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca pārthaḥ prāpya dhanuḥśreṣṭham akṣayyau ca maheṣudhī rathaṃ dhvajaṃ sabhāṃ caiva yudhiṣṭhiram abhāṣata
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Pārtha, having obtained the finest bow, the inexhaustible great quivers, a chariot and banner and the assembly hall, spoke to Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: dhanur astraṃ śarā vīryaṃ pakṣo bhūmir yaśo balam prāptam etan mayā rājan duṣprāpaṃ yad abhīpsitam
english: "O king, I have obtained bow, weapons, arrows, valor, a wing (support), land, glory, and strength — all that was desired and hard to attain has been obtained by me.

sanskrit: tatra kṛtyam ahaṃ manye kośasyāsya vivardhanam karam āhārayiṣyāmi rājñaḥ sarvān nṛpottama
english: In this regard I think the fitting action is to augment this treasury; I will collect tribute from all kings, O best of kings.

sanskrit: vijayāya prayāsyāmi diśaṃ dhanadarakṣitām tithāv atha muhūrte ca nakṣatre ca tathā śive
english: I will set out for conquest in the direction protected by the god of wealth, at an auspicious tithi, muhūrta, and nakṣatra.

sanskrit: dhanaṃjayavacaḥ śrutvā dharmarājo yudhiṣṭhiraḥ snigdhagambhīranādinyā taṃ girā pratyabhāṣata
english: Hearing the words of Dhanaṃjaya, Dharmarāja Yudhiṣṭhira replied to him in a voice both affectionate and deep.

sanskrit: svasti vācyārhato viprān prayāhi bharatarṣabha durhṛdām apraharṣāya suhṛdāṃ nandanāya ca vijayas te dhruvaṃ pārtha priyaṃ kāmam avāpnuhi
english: "Have the worthy brāhmaṇas pronounce blessings and set forth, O bull of the Bhāratas — for the sorrow of enemies and the joy of friends. Victory is certain for you, O Pārtha; obtain what you cherish and desire."

sanskrit: ity uktaḥ prayayau pārthaḥ sainyena mahatā vṛtaḥ agnidattena divyena rathenādbhutakarmaṇā
english: Thus addressed, Pārtha set forth, surrounded by a great army, on the divine chariot Agnidatta, which performed wondrous deeds.

sanskrit: tathaiva bhīmaseno 'pi yamau ca puruṣarṣabhau sasainyāḥ prayayuḥ sarve dharmarājābhipūjitāḥ
english: Likewise Bhīmasena and the twin brothers, those bulls among men, all set out with their armies, duly honored by the Dharma-king.

sanskrit: diśaṃ dhanapater iṣṭām ajayat pākaśāsaniḥ bhīmasenas tathā prācīṃ sahadevas tu dakṣiṇām
english: The son of Pākaśāsana (Arjuna) conquered the direction beloved of the lord of wealth (the north); Bhīmasena likewise the east, and Sahadeva the south.

sanskrit: pratīcīṃ nakulo rājan diśaṃ vyajayad astravit khāṇḍavaprastham adhyāste dharmarājo yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: Nakula, skilled in weapons, conquered the western direction, O king; Dharmarāja Yudhiṣṭhira remained dwelling at Khāṇḍavaprastha.

sanskrit: janamejaya uvāca diśām abhijayaṃ brahman vistareṇānukīrtaya na hi tṛpyāmi pūrveṣāṃ śṛṇvānaś caritaṃ mahat
english: Janamejaya said: O brāhmaṇa, narrate in detail the conquest of the directions; I am not satisfied hearing of the great deeds of my ancestors.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca dhanaṃjayasya vakṣyāmi vijayaṃ pūrvam eva te yaugapadyena pārthair hi vijiteyaṃ vasuṃdharā
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: I will narrate to you the victory of Dhanaṃjaya first; for the earth was conquered by the Pārthas simultaneously.

sanskrit: pūrvaṃ kuṇindaviṣaye vaśe cakre mahīpatīn dhanaṃjayo mahābāhur nātitīvreṇa karmaṇā
english: First, in the territory of the Kuṇindas, the mighty-armed Dhanaṃjaya brought the kings under his sway without excessively fierce fighting.

sanskrit: ānartān kālakūṭāṃś ca kuṇindāṃś ca vijitya saḥ sumaṇḍalaṃ pāpajitaṃ kṛtavān anusainikam
english: Conquering the Ānartās, the Kālakūṭas, and the Kuṇindas, he made Sumaṇḍala and Pāpajit followers with their armies.

sanskrit: sa tena sahito rājan savyasācī paraṃtapaḥ vijigye sakalaṃ dvīpaṃ prativindhyaṃ ca pārthivam
english: Together with them, O king, Savyasācī the scorcher of foes conquered the entire island and the king Prativindhya.

sanskrit: sakaladvīpavāsāṃś ca saptadvīpe ca ye nṛpāḥ arjunasya ca sainyānāṃ vigrahas tumulo 'bhavat
english: Against the inhabitants of the whole island and the kings of the seven islands, a tremendous conflict arose with Arjuna's armies.

sanskrit: sa tān api maheṣvāso vijitya bharatarṣabha tair eva sahitaḥ sarvaiḥ prāgjyotiṣam upādravat
english: The great archer, having conquered them too, O bull of the Bhāratas, then advanced upon Prāgjyotiṣa together with all of them.

sanskrit: tatra rājā mahān āsīd bhagadatto viśāṃ pate tenāsīt sumahad yuddhaṃ pāṇḍavasya mahātmanaḥ
english: There was a great king there, Bhagadatta, O lord of the people; with him there was an immense battle with the great-souled Pāṇḍava.

sanskrit: sa kirātaiś ca cīnaiś ca vṛtaḥ prāgjyotiṣo 'bhavat anyaiś ca bahubhir yodhaiḥ sāgarānūpavāsibhiḥ
english: Surrounded by Kirātas and Cīnas, the king of Prāgjyotiṣa stood, along with many other warriors dwelling along the ocean shores.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa divasān aṣṭau yodhayitvā dhanaṃjayam prahasann abravīd rājā saṃgrāme vigataklamaḥ
english: Then, after fighting with Dhanaṃjaya for eight days, the king, free from fatigue in battle, spoke smiling:

sanskrit: upapannaṃ mahābāho tvayi pāṇḍavanandana pākaśāsanadāyāde vīryam āhavaśobhini
english: "It is fitting, O mighty-armed one, O joy of the Pāṇḍavas, O heir of Pākaśāsana, that such valor adorns you in battle.

sanskrit: ahaṃ sakhā surendrasya śakrād anavamo raṇe na ca śaknomi te tāta sthātuṃ pramukhato yudhi
english: I am the friend of the lord of the gods, not inferior to Indra in battle, and yet I cannot stand before you in combat, my son.

sanskrit: kim īpsitaṃ pāṇḍaveya brūhi kiṃ karavāṇi te yad vakṣyasi mahābāho tat kariṣyāmi putraka
english: What do you desire, O son of Pāṇḍu? Speak — what shall I do for you? Whatever you say, O mighty-armed one, that I shall do, my son."

sanskrit: arjuna uvāca kurūṇām ṛṣabho rājā dharmaputro yudhiṣṭhiraḥ tasya pārthivatām īpse karas tasmai pradīyatām
english: Arjuna said: "The bull of the Kurus, King Yudhiṣṭhira the son of Dharma — I desire sovereignty for him; let tribute be paid to him."

sanskrit: bhavān pitṛsakhā caiva prīyamāṇo mayāpi ca tato nājñāpayāmi tvāṃ prītipūrvaṃ pradīyatām
english: "You are a friend of my father, and are dear to me as well; therefore I do not command you — with affection, let it be given."

sanskrit: bhagadatta uvāca kuntīmātar yathā me tvaṃ tathā rājā yudhiṣṭhiraḥ sarvam etat kariṣyāmi kiṃ cānyat karavāṇi te
english: Bhagadatta said: "As you are like a son of Kuntī to me, so is King Yudhiṣṭhira; all of this I shall do — what else shall I do for you?"

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca taṃ vijitya mahābāhuḥ kuntīputro dhanaṃjayaḥ prayayāv uttarāṃ tasmād diśaṃ dhanadapālitām
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having conquered him, the mighty-armed Dhanaṃjaya, son of Kuntī, proceeded northward from there, to the direction protected by Dhana-da (Kubera).

sanskrit: antargiriṃ ca kaunteyas tathaiva ca bahirgirim tathoparigiriṃ caiva vijigye puruṣarṣabhaḥ
english: The son of Kuntī, that bull among men, conquered the inner mountain region, the outer mountain region, and likewise the region above the mountains.

sanskrit: vijitya parvatān sarvān ye ca tatra narādhipāḥ tān vaśe sthāpayitvā sa ratnāny ādāya sarvaśaḥ
english: Conquering all the mountain regions and the lords of men there, placing them under his sway, he took their jewels in their entirety.

sanskrit: tair eva sahitaḥ sarvair anurajya ca tān nṛpān kulūtavāsinaṃ rājan bṛhantam upajagmivān
english: Together with all of them, having won the affection of those kings, he then, O king, advanced upon Bṛhanta, the dweller in the Kulūta region.

sanskrit: mṛdaṅgavaranādena rathanemisvanena ca hastināṃ ca ninādena kampayan vasudhām imām
english: Shaking this earth with the excellent sound of mṛdaṅga drums, the rumble of chariot wheels, and the trumpeting of elephants —

sanskrit: tato bṛhantas taruṇo balena caturaṅgiṇā niṣkramya nagarāt tasmād yodhayām āsa pāṇḍavam
english: Then the young Bṛhanta, with a four-division army, sallied forth from that city and engaged the Pāṇḍava in battle.

sanskrit: sumahān saṃnipāto 'bhūd dhanaṃjayabṛhantayoḥ na śaśāka bṛhantas tu soḍhuṃ pāṇḍavavikramam
english: There was an immense clash between Dhanaṃjaya and Bṛhanta, but Bṛhanta was unable to withstand the Pāṇḍava's valor.

sanskrit: so 'viṣahyatamaṃ jñātvā kaunteyaṃ parvateśvaraḥ upāvartata durmedhā ratnāny ādāya sarvaśaḥ
english: Knowing the son of Kuntī to be most irresistible, that lord of the mountain, of poor judgment, turned back, taking all his jewels with him.
